Root shading produces blunt oval-looking terminal regions, but the actual starting-cap marker is not visible in the diagnostic; this appearance alone is not evidence of exposed cut caps or disconnected geometry.

The upper anterior root meets the forehead region; a continuous arc sweeps over/behind the ear, descends at the back and returns forward below the ear toward a short upward cheek-adjacent tip. The ear remains visible inside the curl. No obvious floating segment or break. Root transition is visually abrupt and rounded, with little material integration against the flat white head, but this is a refinement concern rather than demonstrated failed attachment. Far horn is largely coincident/occluded in this exact side projection; symmetry alone is not a defect.

Head occludes the inward/anterior root regions while posterior descending portions remain visible outside it; this differs credibly from south layering. Visible ear outlines remain distinct. No magenta start cap is visible. Small triangular dark/gray root-side slivers beside upper head are somewhat hard-edged but plausibly exposed horn flank; they do not visibly create a detached base or fore/aft reversal. Forward tip portions are mostly hidden, with narrow lateral slivers; consistent with the authored volume.

Opposite side shows the same continuous forehead-to-back-to-lower-cheek curl and separate ear. No obvious skull/ear penetration or discontinuity in the assembly. Similarity to east is expected for symmetric horns; fixed body differences are not a horn defect. No west cap diagnostic or dedicated west root closeup supplied.
